evals.prompt: Draw an ERD for a small library system: members borrow copies of books, a book can have several authors and an author can write several books, and each loan has a due date and a returned date. Save it as library.mmd in the output folder.
evals.expected_output: library.mmd holds an erDiagram with members, books, authors, copies, and loans, PK and FK markers, a book-author many-to-many through a junction entity (or a many-to-many relationship), due and returned dates on loans, and a label on every relationship. The syntax passes the Step 2 self-check, and the answer does not make mermaid.live the only way to check it.
expectations: Writes library.mmd in the output folder, and its first diagram line is erDiagram
Has entities for members, books, authors, book copies, and loans, with PK and FK markers on the key attributes
Models the book-author many-to-many through a junction entity or a many-to-many relationship
The loan entity has a due date and a returned date attribute
Every relationship line has a label
No label contains an unquoted special character from the Step 1 table, and no node is a bare end
Does not tell the user to paste the diagram into mermaid.live as the only way to check it

evals.prompt: Make a sequence diagram of the OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow with PKCE between the user's browser, our single-page app, the authorization server, and our API, and give me an SVG of it in the output folder.
evals.expected_output: A .mmd file and, when mermaid-cli can run, an .svg rendered from it in the output folder, both headless. The diagram shows the code verifier and challenge, the authorization request, the redirect with the code, the token exchange with the verifier, and the API call with the access token. If neither mmdc nor npx can run, the answer says the SVG was not rendered, why, and gives the command to run, along with the Mermaid code.
expectations: Writes the diagram as a .mmd file in the output folder, and its first diagram line is sequenceDiagram
Shows the code_verifier and code_challenge, the authorization request, the redirect with the authorization code, the token request carrying the verifier, and the API call with the access token
Participant names that contain spaces are quoted or given aliases
Renders with mmdc, or with npx -y -p @mermaid-js/mermaid-cli mmdc, and writes an .svg to the output folder; or, if neither can run, says the SVG was not rendered, why, and gives the command to run
When a render fails with a parse error, fixes the diagram and renders again instead of handing the error to the user
Never makes opening a browser or mermaid.live the only way to get the image

evals.prompt:
This flowchart doesn't render, fix it:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Start] --> B(Check cache (redis))
    B -->|hit| C[Return value: 100%]
    B -->|miss| D[Query DB]
    D --> end
    C --> end
```
evals.expected_output: A corrected flowchart in a mermaid code block: the label with nested parentheses and the label with % are quoted, and the bare end node is replaced by a quoted or renamed node, while every node, edge, and edge label is kept. Each fix is named in one line, and the user is not asked to fix the syntax.
expectations: Quotes the label with nested parentheses, for example B("Check cache (redis)")
Replaces the bare end target with a quoted or renamed node, for example End["end"] or Done
Keeps every original node and edge, including the hit and miss edge labels
Outputs the corrected diagram in a mermaid code block and names each fix
Does not ask the user to fix the syntax
